When noisy labels meet class imbalance on graphs: A graph augmentation method with LLM and pseudo label
abstract: Class-imbalanced graph node classification is a practical yet underexplored research problem. Although recent studies have attempted to address this issue, they typically assume clean and reliable labels when processing class-imbalanced graphs. This assumption often violates the nature of real-world graphs, where labels frequently contain noise. Given this gap, this paper systematically investigates robust node classification for class-imbalanced graphs with noisy labels. We propose GraphALP, a novel Graph Augmentation framework based on Large language models (LLMs) and Pseudo-labeling techniques. Specifically, we design an LLM-based oversampling method to generate synthetic minority nodes, producing label-accurate minority nodes to alleviate class imbalance. Based on the class-balanced graphs, we develop a dynamically weighted pseudo-labeling method to obtain high-confidence pseudo labels to reduce label noise ratio. Additionally, we implement a secondary LLM-guided oversampling mechanism to mitigate potential class distribution skew caused by pseudo labels. Experimental results show that GraphALP achieves superior performance over state-of-the-art methods on class-imbalanced graphs with noisy labels.

title: A taxonomy of interpretable neurosymbolic models for time series classification
abstract: Time series classification (TSC) with deep learning has advanced markedly over the last decade, yet the mechanisms by which models identify and exploit discriminative patterns remain only partially understood, limiting interpretability. This paper surveys neuro-symbolic approaches that aim either (i) to derive knowledge—by extracting human-readable rules and explanations from data—or (ii) to use knowledge—by injecting logical, physical, or structural constraints into learning. We review methods spanning Signal Temporal Logic (STL) formula extraction and temporal decision trees, neuro-symbolic constraint synthesis and circuits, loss-based regularization including physics-informed objectives, probabilistic logic for event reasoning (e.g., DeepProbLog), and concept-level continual learning and distillation. We position these methods along common axes—explicit vs. implicit knowledge, applicability to TSC, capacity for knowledge discovery, prior knowledge requirements, and reproducibility—and discuss typical failure modes, including data bias and reasoning shortcuts. We also relate recent frugalityoriented designs that leverage non-trainable filters without sacrificing accuracy. Our analysis indicates that neurosymbolic techniques can provide actionable explanations and stronger inductive bias, with especially strong results on binary tasks, but face challenges in scaling to multi-class settings, handling shape-dependent phenomena, and ensuring transparent selection of learned rules. The survey offers a taxonomy and practical guidance for integrating symbolic structure with deep learning in TSC, highlighting open problems and promising directions.

title: Beyond intuition: Zero-shot policy synthesis and execution for temporal knowledge graph question answering
Explainable multi-sensor fusion for robot movement classification using genetic programming-based symbolic expressions
abstract: Accurate robot movement classification is essential for improving the reliability and safety of autonomous systems, especially in dynamic environments where precise motion decisions support task execution and collision avoidance. Multi-sensor data fusion can improve classification robustness by combining complementary information from multiple sensors. However, many high-performing classification models remain difficult to interpret, which limits their use in applications where transparent decision-making is required. This study proposes an explainable classification framework based on genetic programming symbolic classification (GPSC) for multi-sensor robot movement classification. A publicly available dataset collected from 24 ultrasound sensors mounted on the SCITOS G5 mobile robot is used to classify five movement types: forward motion, slight left turn, slight right turn, sharp left turn, and sharp right turn. To address class imbalance and preprocessing sensitivity, several oversampling methods and six scaling/normalization strategies are evaluated. GPSC models are optimized using random hyperparameter value search and assessed using stratified 5-fold cross-validation. The best symbolic expressions are selected using accuracy (ACC), balanced accuracy (BACC), precision, recall, F1-score, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), and matthews correlation coefficient (MCC). Threshold-based voting ensembles (TBVEs) are then constructed from the top symbolic expressions to improve robustness across dataset variations. The results show that the proposed TBVEs achieve perfect classification performance across all evaluation metrics. More importantly, the generated symbolic expressions provide explicit mathematical representations of sensor relationships, supporting transparent analysis of robot movement patterns. The proposed framework therefore offers an accurate and interpretable solution for multi-sensor robotic motion classification.

title: A knowledge-aware graph-based framework for document-level event extraction
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of document-level event extraction as a critical step toward automated knowledge acquisition for intelligent systems. Extracting structured event knowledge from unstructured text is essential for downstream knowledge-based applications such as knowledge graph construction, decision support, and intelligent question answering. However, existing approaches struggle to effectively capture long-range dependencies and complex inter-event relationships within documents while maintaining computational efficiency. To address these challenges, we propose a novel knowledge-aware framework, the Graph Convolutional Network with Pseudo-trigger Combination Recognition(GCN-PCR). The proposed model explicitly represents entities, mentions, and sentences as interconnected nodes in a relational graph, enabling structured modeling of semantic dependencies and co-reference information across document contexts. Furthermore, the pseudo-trigger combination strategy enhances the identification of event structures by improving the robustness of event boundary detection and argument association. Extensive experiments on two public datasets demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods. More importantly, our framework provides a scalable and effective solution for transforming unstructured textual data into structured event knowledge, facilitating its integration into knowledge-based systems.

title: Spectral graph contrastive learning via adaptive adjacent-order residual injection
A Performance-Guided Framework for retinal vessel segmentation
abstract: Accurate retinal vessel segmentation requires reliable delineation of fine and low-contrast vascular structures. However, conventional supervised training often treats all image regions equally despite substantial spatial variations in segmentation performance. To address this limitation, we propose a Performance-Guided Framework (PGF) for retinal vessel segmentation. PGF first trains a baseline model and estimates patch-level segmentation performance using Dice scores. Based on the resulting performance ranking, a performance-guided data reconstruction strategy selectively masks high-performing regions, thereby focusing training on more challenging areas. Then, the optimization stage employs a dual-objective learning scheme, combining direct segmentation supervision on retained regions with selective knowledge distillation on masked regions to preserve prediction consistency. Extensive experiments on four public retinal vessel datasets (DRIVE, STARE, CHASE_DB1, and ROSSA) demonstrate its effectiveness. Using a standard U-Net backbone, PGF achieves Dice scores of 79.57%, 77.55%, 76.44%, and 91.01%, respectively, outperforming competing methods across all datasets. Moreover, PGF consistently improves multiple backbone networks and enables a standard U-Net to achieve performance comparable to, or better than, substantially more complex architectures without introducing additional inference overhead. These results demonstrate that PGF is an effective, generalizable, and architecture-agnostic training framework for retinal vessel segmentation.

title: Privacy-preserving federated learning AdaBoost via knowledge distillation
abstract: There are many scenarios where different entities would like to share their knowledge through building a joint machine learning model for a common goal. Federated learning arises to solve such problems when the data privacy of each entity is imposed as an essential requirement. Although much work has been done in applying deep learning networks to federated learning scenarios, scarce effort has been made to adapt other classic and lighter machine learning algorithms to the aforementioned problem. This paper presents an adaptation of the AdaBoost ensemble method to federated scenarios, using ensemble knowledge distillation. To do so, in each iteration, the clients build a model using their local data and send the predictions over a small unlabeled public dataset to the server, thus keeping their sensitive information private. Then, the server aggregates these predictions and creates a model using the public data, sending it back to all the clients. The paper also presents and analyzes several versions of such an algorithm. The performance of the proposed method has been tested using 14 datasets, three evaluation metrics, and four data distribution scenarios. It demonstrates significantly better performance than other state-of-the-art methods, better privacy protection, and robustness against adversarial attacks on the network.

PAMA: Dual-memory augmentation assisted pseudo-anomaly contrastive learning for multivariate time series anomaly detection
abstract: For multivariate time series anomaly detection, most methods assume that training data are clean and ignore the characteristics of anomalous data. They often suffer from the overgeneralization problem during the reconstruction process. To address these problems, dual-memory augmentation assisted pseudo-anomaly contrastive learning for multivariate time series anomaly detection (shorted as PAMA) is proposed. First, the prior knowledge of anomalies is utilized to generate pseudo anomalies from the original time series. The normal and pseudo-anomalous feature representations that contain global and local information are respectively achieved by the global and local encoders. Two independent memory modules are constructed to further memorize normal and pseudo-anomalous prototypes. Second, a dual-memory augmentation mechanism is proposed to conduct data augmentation upon the normal and pseudo-anomalous feature representations and then obtain the memory-augmented feature representations. Third, the pseudo-anomaly contrastive learning is proposed to perform temporal contrastive learning and instance contrastive learning on the obtained memory-augmented representations. Compared with the fourteen baseline methods, the experimental results demonstrate that PAMA achieves the optimal detection performance.

title: Towards Federated Long-Tailed Graph Learning: An energy-guided dual decoupling approach
abstract: Federated Graph Learning facilitates collaborative graph modeling across distributed clients while preserving data privacy.However, real-world data categories frequently exhibit long-tailed distributions. Such statistical scarcity severely degrades performance in two ways: it biases the global model toward majority classes, and it structurally isolates minority nodes by submerging them in heterophilic, head-dominated neighborhoods.While existing methods attempt topology-agnostic statistical compensations, they often fail under data scarcity.Instead of recovering tail nodes, they overfit the structural noise from adjacent dominant classes, leading to representation degradation.To address these limitations, we propose FedEPD, a framework built on a dual decoupling paradigm that separates topological purification from semantic recalibration.Specifically, FedEPD utilizes distribution-aware Dirichlet energy pruning to filter spatial heterophilic edges. It then overcomes Non-IID distribution shifts by extracting robust global prototypes from topologically central nodes, which are incorporated into local representations via a spatial low-pass prototype injection. Furthermore, a two-stage alternating optimization strategy strictly protects majority decision boundaries while improving minority accuracy.Extensive experiments demonstrate that FedEPD achieves state-of-the-art performance across diverse long-tailed benchmarks, yielding absolute improvements of up to 4.97\% in Accuracy and 5.48% in Macro-F1.

Rule-based semantic hypergraph parsing from textual annotations
abstract: A semantic hypergraph is a knowledge representation capable of capturing the hierarchical and multi-relational structures essential in natural language. This paper introduces a rule-based semantic hypergraph parser that transforms textual annotations (dependency trees, semantic roles, coreferences) into a semantic hypergraph. The semantic hypergraph parser preserves nested semantic relationships through recursive and ordered hyperedges, integrating predicate-argument structures and coreferences directly into its hypergraph structure. The input textual annotations, the resulting semantic hypergraph representation, and the rule-based transformations applied during parsing are described in detail. The semantic hypergraph parser is evaluated against an existing parser. The qualitative comparison revealed our parser's strengths in handling adverbial modifiers, adjectival clauses, and coreferences. Quantitative evaluation was performed on two datasets: a large-scale corpus of annotated natural language texts, and a manually curated dataset with gold-standard hypergraph annotations. The results show that our parser output achieves almost perfect alignment with gold annotations, outperforming the existing parser by 3–18% on nested representations. After eliminating baseline differences, statistical significance testing confirmed that these improvements were robust across syntactic constructions. We have publicly released our parser to support research on structured semantic representation and to enable practical artificial intelligence applications, including semantic parsing, text mining, and knowledge extraction.

PillarTrack: Boosting pillar representation for transformer-based 3D single object tracking on point clouds
abstract: LiDAR-based 3D single object tracking (3D SOT) is a critical issue in robotics and autonomous driving. Existing 3D SOT methods typically adhere to a point-based processing pipeline, wherein the re-sampling operation invariably leads to either redundant or missing information, thereby impacting performance. To address these issues, we propose PillarTrack, a novel pillar-based 3D SOT framework. First, we transform sparse point clouds into dense pillars to preserve the local and global geometrics. Second, we propose a Pyramid-Encoded Pillar Feature Encoder (PE-PFE) design to enhance the robustness of pillar feature for translation/rotation/scale. Third, we present an efficient Transformer-based backbone from the perspective of modality differences. Finally, we construct our PillarTrack based on above designs. Extensive experiments show that our method achieves comparable performance on the KITTI and NuScenes datasets, significantly enhancing the performance of the baseline.

Seeing the unseen: Cognitive Visual Imagination for camouflaged object detection
abstract: Camouflaged object detection (COD) aims to segment objects that are seamlessly embedded in their surroundings. However, existing models still struggle with extreme camouflage, where local textures are nearly indistinguishable from the background. Motivated by a cognitive analogy, in which observers reduce perceptual ambiguity by imagining a plausible target appearance before verification, we propose a Cognitive Visual Imagination (CVI) framework. CVI is divided into two stages: (1) Mental Template Generation, which uses the generative prior of a frozen pre-trained image editing foundation model to create a cognitive template that highlights the target while suppressing background distractions; and (2) CVINet, a dual-stream segmentation network that combines the original image with the generated template. To bridge low-level visual cues and high-level cognitive priors, CVINet uses a weight-sharing encoder to extract multi-scale features and introduces two modules inspired by complementary perceptual processes: (i) the cognitive semantic injection (CSI) module, which adaptively injects high-level semantic cues based on cross-stream feature discrepancies, motivated by contrastive perception, and (ii) the cognitive structure refinement (CSR) module, which uses high-frequency priors to bolster structural details and refine object boundaries, analogous to boundary confirmation. Extensive experiments with four widely used COD benchmark datasets show competitive performance. By operationalizing a cognitively inspired “imagine-to-verify” workflow, this study provides an effective and practical approach to camouflaged object detection. The source code will be made publicly available upon acceptance.

title: KnowCL: A Universal Knowledge Embedded Contrastive Learning framework for hyperspectral image classification
abstract: Hyperspectral image (HSI) classification techniques have been intensively studied and a variety of models have been developed. However, these HSI classification models are confined to pocket models and unrealistic ways of dataset partitioning. The former limits the generalization performance of the model and the latter is partitioned leading to inflated model evaluation metrics, which results in plummeting model performance in the real world. Therefore, we propose a universal knowledge embedded contrastive learning framework (KnowCL) for supervised, unsupervised, and semisupervised HSI classification, which largely closes the gap between HSI classification models between pocket models and standard vision backbones. We present a new HSI processing pipeline in conjunction with a range of data transformation and augmentation techniques that provide diverse data representations and realistic data partitioning. The proposed framework based on this pipeline is compatible with all kinds of backbones and can fully exploit labeled and unlabeled samples with the expected training time. Furthermore, we design a new loss function, which can adaptively fuse the supervised loss and unsupervised loss, enhancing the learning performance. This proposed new classification paradigm shows great potential in exploring for HSI classification technology. The code can be accessed at \url{https://github.com/quanweiliu/KnowCL}.

Graph-structured neighborhood shaping: A topology-aware graph-based mechanism for engineering optimization
abstract: The fitness landscapes of complex optimization problems typically exhibit highly non-convex and multimodal characteristics. When addressing such problems, Metaheuristic Algorithms (MHs) frequently experience blind wandering and fall into evolutionary stagnation due to the neglect of local geometric structures. Therefore, this paper proposes Graph-Structured Neighborhood Shaping (GSNS), a plug-and-play correction strategy designed to enhance existing MHs rather than operate as an independent optimizer. In each iteration, the baseline MH first generates tentative candidate positions according to its original search mechanism, after which GSNS reconstructs population neighborhood relationships and applies topology-aware corrections to these tentative positions without replacing the intrinsic update rule of the baseline optimizer. This model utilizes feature distances to establish a dynamic neighborhood graph for regulating information exchange, and integrates a rank-correlated gating unit to adaptively allocate evolutionary weights based on spatial centrifugal degree and evolutionary potential. Furthermore, this mechanism integrates the local mean center and global elite guidance to output correction paths with high confidence. After integrating GSNS into six different MHs, comprehensive validations were conducted on three CEC test suites and 12 engineering optimization problems. The results demonstrate that this topology-aware strategy improves the convergence accuracy and stability of the basic frameworks, effectively enhancing the optimization performance of the optimizers in complex landscapes. The source code can be accessed at: https://drive.mathworks.com/sharing/e8d9a42b-aa9e-4045-bacd-b54b716a8a92.

Scalable multi-objective graph layout via phase-wise optimizations
abstract: Graph layout is a core problem in graph visualization, aiming to produce readable and aesthetically pleasing layouts under multiple, often conflicting, aesthetic objectives. Existing methods, including learning-based approaches, commonly rely on weighted loss fusion, which often leads to optimization conflicts, unstable training, and high computational cost.In this work, we reformulate graph layout generation as a multi-objective optimization problem and propose a \emph{phase-wise multi-objective optimization} (PMO) approach. PMO decomposes multi-objective learning into sequential single-objective training phases, effectively mitigating gradient interference and stabilizing optimization.Based on PMO, we develop a GNN-based layout framework that achieves strong and well-balanced layout quality across multiple aesthetic targets while significantly reducing training time and computational resources. Furthermore, we show that the training cost scales linearly with the number of optimized objectives, demonstrating favorable model capacity and scalability.

Algebraic invariant multilayer-network edge regression: Multi-source data fusion with macro-shock immunity
abstract: Various methods have been proposed to study internode interactions, but several deficiencies have been noted in certain concepts in the literature. This study introduces Algebraic Invariant Multilayer-Network Edge Regression (AIMNER), released as a Stata package to address these deficiencies. The flow and interaction templates apply the competing-destinations principle of spatial interaction theory, computing each edge as a share of the source total so that the alternatives enter every edge weight. The attribute template applies the compositional log-ratio, which compares the two endpoint attributes in relative rather than absolute terms. Since the edges are homogeneous of degree zero, they are algebraically invariant to uniform positive multiplicative macro shocks. The property is confined to this class of shocks: it does not cover heterogeneous regional shocks, asymmetric corridor shocks, nonlinear structural breaks, or channel-specific measurement error. The closed-form structure allows the framework to scale to large networks. The framework preserves the heterogeneity of each source-destination edge. The recalculation structure over periods, which includes all interactions within the closed interaction set of network edges, makes the framework applicable to dynamic networks. Since the framework operates at the feature level, it is not dependent on any estimator. The chosen estimator may use instruments for identification and clustered standard errors for inference. Together, these properties make AIMNER a feature-level multi-source data fusion framework that is, in principle, transferable to other systems with directed flows and node attributes. The framework is tested in the context of interprovincial job-seeking migration within Türkiye. Because the evidence comes from a single relational system, transfer to other networked processes is stated as a potential application rather than a demonstrated result. The results obtained in the application are consistent with the literature, showing that birthplace-based social ties are the dominant positive channel. At the same time, unemployment and educational differences function as attribute-based push-pull constraints. In the non-absorbed instrumental variables (IV) benchmark specification, the highway-distance coefficient is negative and smaller in absolute magnitude than the birthplace coefficient.

title: HuddsTrafficFL: A benchmark testbed and dataset for Byzantine-robust federated learning in urban traffic systems
abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training without sharing raw data, making it suitable for privacy-sensitive applications such as intelligent transportation systems and distributed Internet of Things (IoT) environments. However, evaluating Byzantine-resilient FL under realistic deployment conditions remains challenging. Existing benchmark datasets are mainly based on image classification or generic network intrusion tasks and often fail to capture geographically distributed clients, naturally occurring non-IID data, sensor-derived anomaly labels, and integrated Byzantine attack evaluation within a unified framework. To address this limitation, we present HuddsTrafficFL , a reproducible benchmark dataset and evaluation framework developed from a city-scale traffic sensing environment using SUMO/TraCI simulations and OpenStreetMap road networks. HuddsTrafficFL provides three core contributions: (1) a geographically grounded federated learning dataset containing 91,482 timestep observations collected from 292 clients, capturing natural non-IID characteristics and heterogeneous data distributions; (2) sensor-derived anomaly labels generated directly from junction-level traffic behaviour, including sudden speed reductions and abnormal queue growth patterns; and (3) a configurable Byzantine attack and defence evaluation pipeline that enables reproducible robustness assessment across multiple datasets. To the best of our knowledge, HuddsTrafficFL is the first benchmark that simultaneously integrates geographically grounded FL clients, sensor-derived anomaly labels, natural non-IID data characteristics, and Byzantine attack evaluation within a single reproducible environment. We evaluate four representative Byzantine attacks and three aggregation strategies: FedAvg (undefended baseline), Krum and Coordinate Median (robust methods) across HuddsTrafficFL, CICIDS2017, and BoT-IoT. Experimental results show that standard FedAvg achieves an AUC of 0.6706 under model poisoning with a 25% attacker fraction per round, whereas coordinate median consistently achieves an AUC of at least 0.9874 across all evaluated attack-dataset combinations. The baseline federated model on HuddsTrafficFL achieves an AUC of 0.9683, demonstrating that the benchmark provides realistic learning conditions and meaningful robustness evaluation. The dataset, simulation pipeline, interactive dashboard, and benchmark scripts will be publicly released to support reproducible research on secure federated learning for intelligent transportation systems and distributed sensing applications.

RIM: A Retrieval-In-Matching framework for cross-domain global visual localization of UAVs
abstract: Global visual localization of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) using remote-sensing reference maps has attracted increasing attention. However, differences in acquisition time and imaging platform between UAV and reference imagery introduce substantial cross-domain appearance and viewpoint shifts, challenging robust six-degree-of-freedom (6-DoF) pose estimation. To mitigate these shifts, we render UAV-viewpoint references from Google 3D Tiles across locations, altitudes, and orientations. A two-stage strategy adapts SALAD with pose-near positives and geographically distant hard negatives; local geometric consistency then re-ranks the Top-K candidates. We further propose Retrieval-In-Matching (RIM), which freezes the adapted DINOv2-B retriever and distills a local-descriptor decoder from its token field and a shallow VGG19 detail stream. One query-side DINOv2-B backbone forward therefore supports both SALAD retrieval and local description, eliminating a second foundation-model backbone while preserving the retrieval descriptors by construction. We evaluate RIM zero-shot on the reconstructed EPFL Urbanscape and self-collected Chang'an Park datasets, both geographically disjoint from the training data. RIM outperforms ten retrieval baselines. Under the full 3D distance metric at 25/50 m, it improves Recall@1 over SALAD by 8.55/13.77 percentage points on EPFL and 4.45/8.94 points on Park. At Top-K=5, the measured online query path through retrieval, candidate matching, and robust geometric verification takes 90.8 ms: 1.2 times faster than the strongest separate sparse-matching baseline and over 30 times faster than RoMa, while maintaining comparable re-ranking accuracy. These results demonstrate an efficient UAV global visual localization pipeline under unreliable satellite navigation. The source code is available at https://github.com/curious-energy/RIM.

SurveyAgent-HKA: A multi-agent framework for scientific survey generation with LLMs and human knowledge augmentation
abstract: Automatic scientific survey generation has become an important task in scientific document processing. The common approach of retrieving literature from a single source (e.g., arXiv) and generating surveys through a one-pass large language model (LLM) call, often leads to limited reference coverage and, more importantly, fails to replicate the expert-driven revision process that is crucial for writing high-quality surveys. In this paper, we introduce a multi-agent framework for improving the quality of end-to-end scientific survey generation with LLMs, augmented by knowledge derived from published surveys and real-world peer review comments of survey papers. The framework decomposes survey generation into a sequence of well-defined sub-tasks, each handled by an LLM-powered agent. A unified literature retrieval pipeline first gathers relevant papers from multiple sources and identifies key topics through clustering, which is then used to generate an initial survey structure. This structure is further refined by incorporating the human-written outline from relevant published surveys. Based on the refined outline, topic-focused papers are collected and re-ranked to select a representative set for drafting a well-grounded survey draft. Then, we identify common issues raised by experts in peer comments from published surveys to guide the revisions and finalize the survey. Experiments on two domains show that our approach outperforms mainstream baselines in citation quality, structural consistency, and content quality. Furthermore, our framework is efficient in both time and cost, making it a practical solution for broader AI-assisted scientific writing applications.

Evaluating the scalability and adversarial generalization of GRPO-trained NLI models
abstract: Natural Language Inference (NLI) is a central task in natural language understanding with applications in fact-checking, question answering, and information retrieval. Despite its importance, current NLI systems heavily rely on supervised learning with datasets that often contain annotation artifacts and biases, limiting generalization and real-world applicability. In this work, we apply a reinforcement learning-based approach using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) for Chain-of-Thought (CoT) learning in NLI, eliminating the need for human-labeled rationales and enabling this type of training on challenging datasets such as ANLI. We fine-tune 7B, 14B, and 32B language models using parameter-efficient techniques (LoRA and QLoRA), demonstrating strong performance across standard and adversarial NLI benchmarks. At the 32B scale, GRPO-trained models generalize better than other supervised baselines in adversarial sets. With AWQ quantization, the 32B model fits within 22 GB of CUDA memory. This work provides a scalable and practical framework for building robust NLI systems without sacrificing inference quality.

Software-defined radio sensing for self-harming behaviour detection using CWT transformation and deep learning
abstract: Self-harming, prevalent among youths and adolescents, is highly linked to coping difficulties, emotional distress, trauma, and low self-esteem. Such behaviors are a serious problem as regards social well-being, mental health and emotional stability, which are detrimental to individuals, society and healthcare systems. Early detection of self-harming behavior is vital for enabling timely intervention and mitigating long-term psychological risks. In this article, we propose an intelligent human self-harming behavior detection system leveraging Software Defined Radio (SDR) signals-based non-contact platform and deep learning. The proposed system uses a multi-carrier orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) signal to extract wireless channel state information for self-harm detection. It employs the Continuous Wavelet Transform (CWT) to convert raw one-dimensional (1D) OFDM signals into two-dimensional (2D) spectrogram representations, enriching the feature set for deep learning models. A customised convolutional neural network (CNN) is designed to capture abrupt physical movements associated with self-harm while maintaining low computational complexity for real-time deployment. The customised CNN is rigorously evaluated against benchmark pre-trained deep learning models, including AlexNet, ResNet18, and GoogleNet, to demonstrate competitive sensitivity and specificity. Comprehensive comparisons are conducted based on performance metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and computational efficiency parameters. The proposed customised model achieves competitive accuracy (96%) and F1-score (94%) while being significantly more computationally efficient, requiring only 3,305,801 trainable parameters, 12.61 MB of memory, and 45.09 ms inference time.

Minimum Spanning Trees ensemble framework: A geometric classifier
abstract: Classifiers based on the Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) capture complex, non-linear class geometries that elude many standard models, but a single MST is inherently unstable: small changes in the training data can reshape the tree and degrade classification performance. Existing MST-based ensembles address this only partially, either collapsing structural evidence into hard voting decisions or re-analyzing the graph topology at every prediction, limiting scalability and inductive capability. To resolve both limitations, a two-phase framework is introduced that permanently decouples topological analysis from inference. In Phase I, an ensemble of MSTs is built on subsamples drawn with a randomly perturbed class ratio, exposing it to diverse density regimes. A local model is then trained on the pure instances of each subsample, identified through the label homogeneity of the MST neighborhood, and used to infer the affinity of the remaining ambiguous ones, without manual calibration of where the ensemble should specialize. Averaging these local affinities across the ensemble yields a continuous, per-instance affinity score quantifying class membership, replacing hard voting with a graded, ensemble-aggregated measure. In Phase II, this pre-computed score is reused for prediction through interchangeable strategies, such as k-nearest-neighbor interpolation or a dedicated regression model, without ever reconstructing the graph. This separation makes the framework modular, adapting the prediction mechanism to the problem while preserving the topological sensitivity of the underlying MST ensemble.

Affect-conditioned prompt orchestration for mental-health support chatbots: Architecture, ablation analysis, and safety considerations
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for mental-health support, where fluency is both an asset and a risk: a stand-alone model can sound empathic while missing emotional cues, reading sarcasm literally, or leaving discriminatory framing unchallenged. We investigate a modular architecture in which affective and safety signals actively guide an LLM-based support chatbot rather than being logged as passive labels. The prototype couples Gemma 3 4B with classifiers for sentiment, emotion, sarcasm, and hate speech, whose outputs feed a prompt orchestration layer that shapes response tone, intervention style, personalisation, and safety handling, alongside user profiling, short-term memory, and adaptive guidance-mode selection. An ablation-oriented evaluation compares an LLM-only baseline with sentiment-, emotion-, profile-, and hate-speech-conditioned variants and the full system, using a structured response-level rubric with semantic similarity as an auxiliary indicator. Affect conditioning mainly reshapes how responses are framed, most visibly in validation and the handling of discriminatory content, while conditional safety prompting produces the clearest behavioural change; configurations converge on the same concern while diverging in framing and safety stance. The evaluation is exploratory by construction: single generations, one base model, author-applied criteria, and no independent raters, so we report no significance tests and make no claim of clinical efficacy. We also analyse how classifier error propagates into the orchestration layer and specify the human, adversarial, and benchmark-based evaluation such systems require before real-world use. The contribution is an architecture whose determinants are inspectable and separately adjustable, together with the protocol under which it should be judged.

abstract: Open Arabic medical language models trail their English counterparts, while the most capable closed models remain inaccessible for regulated regional deployment, leaving native-Arabic clinical reasoning without a strong, openly deployable model at a practical scale. This paper presents Hakeem-7B, an Arabic medical reasoning model built on TII's Falcon-H1-7B (a parallel Mamba-2/attention hybrid), and asks how far a fixed 7-billion-parameter open model can be pushed on intrinsic Arabic medical capability by post-training recipe alone. On a decontaminated, defect-filtered split of the native-Arabic MedAraBench exam benchmark, a knowledge-first post-training recipe (Domain-Adaptive Pre-Training to Supervised Fine-Tuning to Direct Preference Optimization; DAPT to SFT to DPO) increased the accuracy from 53% to almost 60%, and on a single internally-consistent harness Hakeem-7B beats every other 7-8 B model, its own base, and a dedicated medical 70 B (OpenBioLLM), while tying the 27-32 B band, that is, matching models 4-10x its size. A blind dual-judge panel places its chain-of-thought reasoning above OpenBioLLM-70B and its own base. The central finding is as much methodological as empirical: under a fixed 7 B with no retrieval, the primary driver ofcapability is domain-adaptive pre-training on in-domain knowledge, not reinforcement learning, and the gap to a strong teacher is one of knowledge retention, not reasoning skill. To the authors' knowledge Hakeem-7B is the first decontaminated, matched-controlled, confidence-interval-bounded Arabic medical reasoner at the 7 B scale. Hakeem-7B is available at https://huggingface.co/Vionex-digital/Hakeem-7B.

GInGER: Genetic domain partitioning for interpretable rule extraction and induction
abstract: Symbolic knowledge extraction techniques aim to provide human-interpretable descriptions of predictive models through compact and expressive representations. Among these, approaches based on input domain partitioning offer a natural way to combine local explanations with a global view of the model behaviour. However, existing methods often rely on rigid partitioning strategies, require discretisation of continuous targets, or produce complex and overlapping structures that hinder interpretability. This work introduces GInGER, a framework for symbolic knowledge extraction and rule induction based on the optimisation of input domain partitions. The proposed method identifies non-overlapping hypercubic regions through a genetic search process that directly optimises domain cuts according to a user-defined fitness function. Each region is associated with a symbolic prediction, expressed as a class label, a constant value, or a local linear model, enabling a unified treatment of classification and regression tasks without requiring target discretisation. GInGER can be applied both as a post-hoc explainer, to approximate the behaviour of black-box models, and as an ante-hoc method to directly induce interpretable models from data. An extensive empirical evaluation on multiple classification and regression data sets shows that the proposed approach achieves a favourable trade-off between predictive performance and model compactness, often producing more concise symbolic representations than competing methods while maintaining comparable accuracy.

Intent augmentation contrastive learning for Session-based Social Recommendation
abstract: Session-based Social Recommendation (SSR) aims to enhance next-item predictions by integrating a user's session activities with their social networks, yet it struggles with data sparsity, particularly due to the very limited short-term interactions within sessions.Traditional studies have applied Contrastive Learning (CL) to address this problem, but they typically avoid explicit data augmentations to keep original session sequences intact, considering the sensitivity of short sessions to disturbances.This conservative strategy, however, may limit the diversification of user-item interactions, potentially causing overfitting and generalization problems, and thus inadequately addressing data sparsity in session contexts.In this paper, we propose Intent Augmentation Contrastive Learning (IACL) for SSR, a model-agnostic approach that utilizes dual training objectives for sophisticated intent modeling.It starts with explicit intra-session augmentation to target specific intents and then expands to capture broader high-level intent patterns across sessions with augmented inter-session prototypes.In contrast to traditional strategies that skip augmentation, the core of IACL is its intent augmentation strategy, which offers both intra-session and inter-session perspectives, significantly broadening the model's exposure to various user behaviors and preferences, thus more effectively addressing data sparsity.Moreover, we introduce a denoised encoder module, Personalized Session Encoder with Filter Networks (PFN), which delivers personalized recommendations by incorporating all key features while suppressing noise in the frequency domain.By integrating PFN with IACL, we demonstrate that our approach, PFN-IACL, surpasses existing methods in performance across three datasets.Our code is freely available\footnote{Find our code at \url{https://anonymous.4open.science/r/PFN-IACL-WSDM26-32B5}}.

title: DAMEL: Dual-axis multi-expert learning for class-imbalanced learning
abstract: Various algorithms have been proposed to address the challenges posed by class-imbalanced learning from real-world data with long-tailed distributions. While these algorithms reduce prediction bias through rebalancing techniques, they often introduce increased prediction variance as a trade-off. Several multi-expert learning algorithms aim to address this variance but involve complex procedures. We propose a new multi-expert learning algorithm, called the dual-axis multi-expert learning (DAMEL), which reduces both bias and variance of predictions by using multiple experts along both representation and time axes. Along the representation axis, DAMEL concatenates the representations of multiple experts and trains an auxiliary balanced classifier simultaneously with the concatenated representations. Along the time axis, DAMEL aggregates network weights across training epochs, employing these aggregated weights during testing. Experimental results demonstrate that DAMEL reduces both bias and variance of predictions, highlighting its effectiveness in class-imbalanced learning.

title: Sensory-aware sequential recommendation via review-distilled representations
abstract: Sequential recommenders learn behavioral patterns from item identifiers, while the experiential properties that users describe in reviews, such as how products look, feel, smell, taste, or sound, rarely enter item representations in a controlled, auditable form. We present ASER (Attribute-based Sensory-Enhanced Representation), an offline pipeline that fine-tunes a large language model to extract evidence-grounded sensory attribute-value records, such as color: matte black or scent: vanilla, from review text and distills them into a compact student encoder that produces a frozen five-facet sensory bank for each item catalog. At recommendation time the pretrained backbone stays frozen: a lightweight relational metric between the user history and each candidate is learned over the bank, and its correction is applied within a validation-selected magnitude bound. Across five Amazon domains and four backbones, trained within a common experimental pipeline and evaluated by full-catalog leave-one-out ranking without sampled negatives, this integration improves HR@10 and NDCG@10 in all 20 domain-backbone pairs, with average relative gains of 6.1% and 6.4%. A matched non-sensory control channel, built with the same seed model, schema, and pipeline, separates the sources of the gain: the hit-rate improvement follows from structured, evidence-grounded extraction as such, whereas the sensory vocabulary yields a ranking-quality advantage in eight of nine matched comparisons. An audit of the Beauty evaluation catalog finds that 94.8% of retained records are supported by their cited evidence spans, so the extracted signal remains inspectable against its source text.

Explainable lifelong streaming learning based on Episode-to-Concept formation
abstract: Real-time on-device continual learning applications are used on mobile phones, consumer robots, and smart appliances. Such devices have limited processing and memory storage capabilities, whereas continual learning acquires data over a long period of time. By necessity, lifelong learning algorithms have to be able to operate under such continual lifelong constraints while delivering good performance. In this study, we propose a neuroscience model, the Explainable Lifelong Learning (ExLL) model, inspired by the Episodic-to-Concept (EpCon) theoretical model of hippocampal function in concept learning. ExLL incorporates several important traits: 1) learning to learn, in a single pass, from streaming data with scarce examples and resources; 2) a self-organizing prototype-based architecture that expands as needed, clusters streaming data into separable groups by similarity and preserves data against catastrophic forgetting; 3) an interpretable architecture to convert the clusters into explainable IF-THEN rules as well as to justify model predictions in terms of what is similar and dissimilar to the inference; and 4) inferences at the global and local level using a pairwise decision fusion process to enhance the accuracy of the inference. We compare ExLL against contemporary online learning algorithms, using OpenLoris, F-SIOL-310, and Places datasets to evaluate several continual learning scenarios for video streaming, low-sample learning, scaling, and dealing with imbalanced data. The algorithms are evaluated for their performance in accuracy, number of parameters, and experiment runtime requirements. ExLL outperforms these compared algorithms for accuracy in the majority of the tested scenarios.

R-TVF: A Regularized Time-Varying Fourier method for missing data recovery
abstract: High-precision space photometry enables the continuous monitoring of stellar oscillations, which manifest as variations in stellar flux, known as light curves. However, large data gaps distort the signal’s shape, making time series imputation important for recovering these underlying flux oscillations. Standard interpolation methods fail to reconstruct intrinsic variability. Conversely, traditional harmonic methods (e.g., Dynamic Harmonic Regression, Trigonometric Box–Cox AutoRegressive Moving Average Trend Seasonal, and Frequency-Specific Basic Structural Model) capture periodic patterns but fail to adapt to multi-periodic non-stationary stellar flux variations across large gaps due to the recursive propagation of stochastic parameters and the risk of phase drift. To address this, we propose the Regularized Time-Varying Fourier (R-TVF) method. This frequency-informed algorithm models the signal as a superposition of periodic components with time-varying amplitudes, effectively integrating domain knowledge directly into its structure. We evaluated R-TVF on 72 Delta Scuti stars, subdivided into High-Amplitude Delta Scuti (HADS) and Low-Amplitude Delta Scuti (LADS) stars. Within this specific stellar family, the experimental results demonstrate that R-TVF outperforms state-of-the-art algorithms, achieving a mean R 2 between 0.968 and 0.987 for HADS and between 0.761 and 0.816 for LADS. In terms of performance, R-TVF improves accuracy by 3% to 9% and reduces execution time by 80% to 88% compared to the second-best performing method.

Trust signals in multiplex socio-technical networks: Information-aware load redistribution for cascade resilience
abstract: Relational trust signals are proposed to make load redistribution resilient to overload-driven cascading failures in socio-technical platforms, yet whether they help beyond the extra capacity they add has never been isolated. We answer this with a capacity-controlled decomposition. Framing crowd-shipping as a two-layer multiplex network, we inject a multiplex-centrality relational signal into both capacity buffering and load redistribution (the Social-Aware policy), and test it by Monte Carlo simulation on proxy topologies from two location-based social networks, Gowalla and Brightkite. At matched capacity, the gains attributed to trust are predominantly capacity-mediated: a slack-aware policy on a uniform buffer is significantly better than the trust-based policy on Brightkite, while on Gowalla no significant difference emerges and the equivalence test is inconclusive. Two principles follow. First, alignment: concentrating capacity helps only when redistribution steers load toward the reinforced nodes; otherwise a provable load-concentration limit (the Gravity-Well) centralizes systemic risk at high trust sensitivity. A placement × routing factorial at matched concentration shows degree- and PageRank-based concentration with no significant difference from the relational signal on Brightkite (a small residual on Gowalla): alignment, not the signal, is the primary lever. Second, a conditional value of relational information: with an independent reliability variable, a relational signal improves on non-social concentration only when it encodes operational reliability rather than structural friendship, with gains that grow with that correlation and degrade with estimation noise. These results delineate when relational signals stabilize or destabilize overload cascades, and yield capacity-first, alignment-aware design guidance for resilient socio-technical services.

title: Transparent forecasting with XAI: Improving accuracy and trust in electricity demand prediction
abstract: This research is based on forecasting the net demand for electricity by considering the previous trends. Considering the overall increase in demand for electricity year by year, predicting such a trend plays a crucial role in a country’s development, as it helps make an accurate prediction of future energy consumption and prepare accordingly. The trends will be considered in light of various factors that affect the electricity usage rate. Different algorithms would be applied to a pipeline to predict appropriate results. The algorithms that would be used are XGB followed by Prophet, which is applied with regressors and then is ensembled, and further optimization is performed. Our result is compared against a broad set of classical statistical and machine-learning baselines (ARIMA, linear/ridge/lasso regression, decision tree, random forest, SVR, KNN, and gradient boosting), evaluated both on the full dataset and, separately, on two demand clusters. The model presented in this paper has outperformed all of these baselines. While hybridisations of Prophet with other learners, and of boosting methods with classical time-series components, have each been explored separately in prior work, the contribution of this research is a formalised, cross-validated stacking ensemble of Prophet and XGBoost specifically for national-scale electricity demand, combined with a SHAP-based explainability layer applied to the resulting ensemble, achieving an RMSE of 13.734 on test data. Not only does the proposed model yield better results, but it also provides a method to explain the effect that each parameter has on the outcome. It accurately depicts the magnitude and impact, whether positive or negative, of electricity load consumption, which in turn affects the prediction of the outcome.

Analysing diverse complex open-source images to assess face mask usage for epidemiological studies
abstract: Face masks are an important intervention for controlling the transmission of respiratory infectious diseases, yet measuring mask use at a population level remains challenging. Open-source images from news media, social media, and public websites provide a potentially valuable source of observational data but are difficult to analyse because of crowd density, variable image quality, occlusions, diverse face orientations, and heterogeneous environmental conditions. We developed and evaluated an artificial intelligence (AI) framework for estimating face mask usage from complex open-source images for epidemiological studies. The framework combines face detection, unusable-image filtering, mask classification, and environmental context assessment (indoor versus outdoor) within a single analytical pipeline. To support model development, we created a large annotated database comprising over 200,000 face images labelled as unusable, mask-wearing, or non-mask-wearing, and fine-tuned state-of-the-art deep learning models for classification tasks. The resulting models achieved F1-scores of 0.926 for unusable-image filtering and 0.986 for mask classification. End-to-end evaluation using ten independent crowd images demonstrated low error rates, with only 1.5% of mask classifications requiring correction following manual review and absolute errors in estimated mask usage ranging from −5.2% to +2.3%. Indoor and outdoor environments were correctly identified in all evaluation cases. These findings demonstrate that complex open-source images can be analysed reliably using AI to estimate face mask usage and environmental context, providing a scalable approach for epidemiological research and population-level monitoring of public health behaviours during respiratory disease outbreaks. Ethics: The study has been approved by The University of New South Wales Human Research Ethics Committee (Approval Number: iRECS6116).

abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong performance in data-rich domains such as programming, yet their reliability in engineering tasks remains limited. Circuit analysis, requiring multimodal understanding and precise mathematical reasoning, highlights these challenges. Although Gemini 2.5 Pro has improved capabilities in diagram interpretation and analog-circuit reasoning, it still struggles to consistently solve problems containing both textual descriptions and circuit diagrams. This paper presents an enhanced end-to-end circuit problem-solving framework using Gemini 2.5 Pro as the backbone model for scalable engineering-education applications. We systematically evaluate Gemini 2.5 Pro on undergraduate circuit-analysis problems and characterize two key failure modes: 1) circuit-recognition hallucinations, particularly incorrect source polarity detection, and 2) reasoning-process hallucinations, such as incorrect current direction assumptions. To address recognition errors, we integrate a fine-tuned YOLO detector and OpenCV-based processing to isolate voltage and current sources for polarity re-identification. To mitigate reasoning errors, we introduce an ngspice -driven verification loop that triggers iterative solution refinement with optional human-in-the-loop feedback. On 83 problems, the proposed pipeline achieves 97.59% accuracy versus Gemini’s 79.52% baseline. On four hand-drawn diagram variations, accuracy improves from 60.61%—71.21% to 89.39%—92.42% with statistically significant gains ( p < 0.005 ). An additional evaluation on 43 problems from a different textbook improves accuracy from 58.14% to 83.72%, providing further evidence of cross-textbook generalizability. Error analysis indicates that circuit recognition remains the dominant source of remaining failures, particularly for different diagram representations. These results demonstrate the robustness, scalability, generalizability, and practical applicability of the proposed framework for engineering education and real-world circuit analysis.

Giving stateless agents a sense of time: A reconsolidating episodic–semantic memory architecture
abstract: Stateless agents may retrieve past interactions yet lack an operational sense of time: external memory makes the past available, but does not represent how experience loses accessibility, returns to relevance, or changes meaning. This paper defines that capacity as an episodic–semantic lifecycle governed by importance, elapsed time, recall and evidence. Pragma, developed by the author, stores sessions as episodes whose narratives stay outside the rewrite target, and consolidates recurring regularities into source-linked beliefs. Deterministic salience and decay regulate accessibility; recall and evidence trigger versioned reconsolidation without overwriting recorded events. The architecture is examined in 229 executions spanning four scenarios, four model families and ten executions per condition. The deterministic layer behaves identically in every family: salience, reinforcement and decay reproduce exactly, no belief is admitted without two distinct sources, and the tracked episode returned to the active zone in all 45 executions where it became dormant. The judgements it consumes do not: the same estimate varies by an order of magnitude across families, and that variation alone can decide whether a designed transition occurs. Removing the lifecycle answers the same memory probes equally well at the store sizes these scenarios reach, which delimits where the difference can be sought. Code, stimuli, metadata and traces make every reported transition inspectable. The contribution is an operational definition of temporal continuity, an architecture implementing it, and evidence separating the properties that hold by construction from those that depend on the model. It is not a validation of reliability, semantic correctness or comparative performance.

DualFusion: Dual adaptive fusion for multi-view pedestrian detection via view reliability modeling and channel reweighting
abstract: Multi-view pedestrian detection is crucial for robust perception, as it alleviates occlusions inherent in single-view perception. Recent methods project feature maps from multiple cameras onto a unified bird’ s-eye view (BEV), enabling spatially aligned cross-view fusion. However, most existing methods fuse features uniformly, overlooking two critical aspects: (i) differences in view reliability (e.g., occlusion severity, projection distortion) and (ii) semantic correlations across feature channels (e.g., contours, foot-level cues). These issues lead to noisy aggregation and suboptimal detection accuracy. To address these issues, we propose DualFusion, a Dual Adaptive Fusion framework for robust BEV representation learning. It consists of two complementary modules: the Cross-View Feature Selector (CVFS), a transformer-based encoder that performs implicit reliability-aware cross-view feature refinement, and the Graph-Inspired View-Channel Reweighting (GVCR), which captures joint view-channel dependencies through context pooling and graph-inspired reweighting. Extensive experiments on three public benchmarks demonstrate that DualFusion achieves competitive overall performance and leading results on several key metrics. Ablation studies further confirm the effectiveness of each component. Our method provides a general paradigm for adaptive multi-view fusion, and the code will be released upon acceptance.

abstract: In the integrated circuit industry, the precise etching process control is critical for realizing the ever scaled new devices. The development of etching process faces new challenges and requires efficient etching simulation to gain insights into the etching mechanisms. This paper introduces a self-supervised learning framework for etching profile prediction, in which a cross convolutional neural network (CCNN) is designed to enhance feature learning. The CCNN incorporates profile-oriented lateral convolution and longitudinal convolution to capture spatial and dynamic variations. The core of our approach lies in self-supervised pretraining: an autoencoder is used as a pretext task to pretrain the lateral convolution layers on simulation data, enabling comprehensive and generalized profile representation. The pretrained representations are then fed to the longitudinal convolution layers, cascade combination layers and fully-connected output layer, which are fine-tuned on experimental data to achieve accurate experimental profile prediction. Experimental results validate the effectiveness of the self-supervised learning framework and the CCNN architecture, yielding a reduction in average prediction errors on experimental data from 7.9028 nm to 6.3822 nm. • Bridge the AI modeling gap between simulations and real etching. • Propose an SSL framework for etching modeling. • Introduce CCNN: an SSL friendly network architecture. • MAE is reduced by 19.2% compared with the SOTA CRNN-based method.

abstract: ABSTRACT Under adverse weather and low-light conditions, models based on multi-scale features typically exhibit reduced image contrast, blurred object boundaries, weakened texture details, and insufficient reliability. As a solution, this paper proposes a Degradation-Aware Gated Fusion Detection Network, termed DAGFNet. Built upon the backbone–neck architecture of YOLO, the proposed method preserves the efficiency of single-stage detection while improving the adaptability of the model to complex degradation scenarios from three perspectives: feature enhancement, degradation modelling, and multi-scale fusion. First, a Degradation-Aware Feature Enhancement Network (DAENet) is designed to decompose the input image into low-frequency structural components and high-frequency detail components through Laplacian pyramid decomposition, thereby enhancing object contours, edge textures, and local responses in a targeted manner. Second, a Degradation Prototype Context Encoder (DPCE) is proposed to model image-level degradation states through learnable degradation prototypes, providing degradation-aware contextual priors for subsequent feature modulation. Finally, a Cross-scale Gated Feature Modulation Module (CGFM) is constructed to integrate degradation context with the multi-scale features output by the backbone. By adaptively recalibrating features at different scales, CGFM enhances reliable representations while suppressing degradation-induced interference. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves competitive performance on the evaluated adverse-weather and low-light object detection tasks.

abstract: In this work, we introduce InfoDisent, a hybrid approach that attaches a lightweight, interpretable head to any frozen pretrained backbone. Unlike fully post-hoc explainers, InfoDisent requires a single training pass of this head over the dataset. Therefore it occupies a middle ground between post-hoc and ante-hoc methods, as it merges the flexibility of post-hoc methods with the concept-level modeling capabilities of self-explainable neural networks, such as ProtoPNets. We demonstrate the effectiveness of InfoDisent through computational experiments and user studies across various datasets using modern backbones such as ViTs and convolutional networks. While InfoDisent achieves competitive performance within the class of interpretable models, we observe an accuracy-interpretability trade-off when compared to black-box counterparts, especially visible in CNNs. Notably, InfoDisent generalizes the prototypical parts approach to novel domains (ImageNet).

title: CFM: An efficient framework for footprint matching in crime scenes
D2S2-UI: A diffusion-driven synthetic dataset for UAV semantic segmentation and cross-dataset generalization
abstract: High-quality semantic segmentation is essential for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) applications, enabling precise data interpretation and efficient decision-making across diverse domains. However, the development of robust segmentation models is often constrained by the limited availability of large-scale, well-annotated datasets, which are expensive and labor-intensive to produce. In this work, we introduce D²S²-UI, a novel synthetic UAV dataset designed for generalized aerial semantic segmentation. Rather than relying on traditional rendering, our methodology harnesses the vast visual and semantic knowledge priors embedded within large-scale text-to-image diffusion models. By actively guiding these knowledge priors through structured textual conditioning and class-consistent semantic control, our framework synthesizes large volumes of accurately labeled aerial imagery without requiring manual annotation. This knowledge-driven approach allows us to scale dataset creation while ensuring high label fidelity and scene diversity. Specifically, D²S²-UI features multi-altitude (20m, 60m, 120m) and multi-viewpoint (nadir, high-oblique, low-oblique) coverage, alongside systematically injected variations in environmental conditions (e.g., weather, time of day) and region-specific terrains (e.g., Asian, Arabic, American, Egyptian, European). Experimental results demonstrate that models trained on D²S²-UI achieve substantially better segmentation accuracy compared to those trained on existing synthetic UAV datasets, showcasing strong, effective generalization across multiple real-world UAV benchmarks. The dataset is publicly available at https://github.com/fahad-lateef/UAV-semantic-segmentation-dataset to support further research in aerial scene understanding and UAV-based vision systems.

title: Two-stage reconstruction of hypergraphs with unknown orders from binary dynamical data
Optimization-aware trustworthy AI: A gradient-based multi-objective learning framework
abstract: Trustworthy artificial intelligence (AI) requires learning systems that achieve strong predictive performance while simultaneously satisfying additional objectives such as fairness and explainability. Existing approaches typically evaluate these characteristics after model training or optimize them individually, providing limited support for balancing multiple competing objectives during learning. This paper presents a gradient-based multi-objective learning framework that jointly optimizes predictive performance, fairness, and explainability within a unified optimization process. The proposed framework formulates trustworthy AI as a multi-objective optimization problem in which predictive performance is measured by classification accuracy, fairness is represented through statistical parity difference, and explainability is approximated using model sparsity. Different trade-offs among these objectives are explored through scalarization, producing candidate models corresponding to different optimization preferences. Experiments were conducted on four benchmark datasets covering diverse application domains. The resulting optimization landscapes demonstrate that the three objectives respond differently to changes in the scalarization weights, revealing non-trivial trade-offs rather than a single common empirical optimum. Across the benchmark datasets, representative empirically non-dominated models substantially increased sparsity while maintaining competitive predictive performance, with fairness outcomes varying across datasets. These findings demonstrate that trustworthy AI properties can be incorporated directly into model optimization rather than treated solely as post-hoc evaluation criteria. The proposed framework provides a flexible foundation for optimization-aware trustworthy AI and can accommodate additional trustworthiness objectives that are amenable to gradient-based optimization.

A self-monitoring explainable AI decision-support architecture for pre-publication content decisions in public-sector communication
abstract: AI-based decision-support systems often achieve high predictive performance but remain difficult to use when their outputs are not explainable, monitored, or connected to human action. This paper develops a self-monitoring explainable AI decision-support architecture for pre-publication communication decisions, in which monitoring generates diagnostic signals while resulting actions remain under human control. The architecture combines five layers: pre-decision input construction, XGBoost-based prediction, SHAP-based explanation, residual monitoring, and a knowledge/action layer for human-in-the-loop use. It is evaluated on 10,728 pre-publication content decisions from 16 official public-sector Facebook channels using chronology-preserving validation with train-only preprocessing. Decision-utility analyses show that the model supports ordinal differentiation between lower- and higher-potential posts. The model primarily exploits the recent communication context of the channel, while structural and format-related characteristics provide additional decision-relevant information. Temporal stress testing and residual monitoring show why the system should not be deployed as a static prediction model, but as a monitored decision-support architecture. Thus, the paper contributes a design pattern for transparent, traceable, and human-overseen AI use in dynamic organisational environments, inspired by selected EU AI Act principles.

Stabilizing EM-based quantification under label shift
abstract: Quantification aims to estimate class prevalences in unlabeled data, often under prior probability shift (also known as label shift). A standard and widely adopted approach is the EM-based quantifier (EMQ), which has demonstrated strong performance in many quantification tasks. We propose a unified framework that decomposes EMQ into two modular components: a posterior transformation and a prevalence update rule. This formulation encompasses existing heuristics and enables the systematic exploration of new ones. We evaluate several variants, both known in the quantification literature (e.g., calibration, MAP) and established stabilization techniques adapted from adjacent literatures (e.g., damping, entropy regularization), on standard multiclass datasets. Results show that different modifications yield complementary gains depending on classifier and data properties, offering insights into how EMQ can be adapted to improve its robustness.

title: From unimodal to multimodal deep physiological signal analysis in healthcare: A survey of models, fusion and explainability
abstract: Physiological signal analysis supports objective assessment of emotion, stress, pain, and disease progression in healthcare systems. Early research focused mainly on unimodal signals, which perform well in controlled settings but are often affected by noise, limited contextual information and reduced generalisability. Recent advances have shifted towards multimodal deep learning frameworks that jointly exploit complementary physiological signals to improve performance and clinical relevance. This survey provides a comprehensive review of the transition from unimodal to multimodal deep physiological signal analysis in healthcare and systematically examines commonly used physiological modalities, benchmark datasets and evaluation metrics. The survey further analyses multimodal alignment strategies and fusion techniques, covering early, intermediate, and late fusion paradigms, with an application-oriented discussion spanning emotion recognition, stress detection, pain assessment and other related domains. Particular emphasis is placed on explainable artificial intelligence methods for multimodal physiological models, highlighting modality-level attribution, cross-modal interactions and application-specific interpretability. Finally, it discusses key dataset- and method-related limitations, such as data scarcity, class imbalance, fusion complexity and computational constraints and outlines future research directions related to wearable edge intelligence, privacy-aware learning, enhanced data diversity and quantum-inspired approaches. This survey can be used as a structured reference for researchers and practitioners developing trustworthy multimodal deep learning solutions for next-generation healthcare systems.

Effective training pressure gates recursive knowledge degradation in LLMs: A multi-axis dose–response study
authors: André Carlos Ponce de Leon Ferreira de Carvalho
abstract: Recursive fine-tuning on synthetic data progressively degrades factual knowledge in large language models under common parameter-efficient settings. The conditions governing whether degradation emerges, remains bounded, or can be reversed are not well understood. Through dose–response experiments across three architectures (Qwen 2.5 1.5B, Gemma 3 1B, and Gemma 4 E2B IT), up to ten recursive generations, and three to six seeds per headline condition (Gemma 4 single-seed and therefore exploratory), we map adapter rank, learning rate, and synthetic exposure onto a regime structure with three zones: homeostatic, bounded, and degradative. Increasing rank produces a threshold-like transition within the tested grid; the boundary falls between effective ranks 50 and 88 for Qwen and between 3 and 6 for Gemma 3, a tenfold difference between architectures, and not the same transition type. Learning-rate sweeps under full fine-tuning provide exploratory evidence broadly consistent with the same qualitative pattern, consistent with perturbation magnitude as the operative variable rather than low-rank adaptation specifically. At intermediate capacity ( r = 128 , Qwen), factual retention remains near 90% while output-distribution quality collapses threefold, revealing a dissociation invisible to scalar retention metrics. Pre-registered dose–response experiments show that reducing synthetic exposure by 50% shifts the Qwen system toward the bounded regime (＋9.2 pp at Gen 10, 95% CI [ 6.9,11.6 ] , p < 0.001 ) and improves endpoint retention on Gemma 3 (＋12.9 pp, p = 0.003 ) without reducing the rate of loss. The effective-training-pressure index is an exploratory post-training summary, not validated as a prospective predictor across architectures or datasets. Experiments use 1–2 billion parameter models; generalization to larger scales is not established.

Tuning conventional recommender systems for beyond-accuracy objectives
abstract: Recommender systems (RSs) are at the heart of digital platforms, delivering personalized content and boosting user engagement. Historically, the design of RSs has predominantly focused on maximizing accuracy, often at the expense of equally critical objectives such as long-tail exposure, diversity, novelty, and popularity-bias mitigation. These beyond-accuracy goals support multi-stakeholder interests and ensure ethical, inclusive recommendation outcomes. Although Multi-Objective Recommender Systems (MORSs) offer a conceptual framework for addressing these competing goals, they usually demand major architectural changes, complicating practical deployment. This work investigates whether hyperparameter tuning of traditional accuracy-driven RSs can serve as a pragmatic, model-preserving lever for improving multi-objective behavior without requiring immediate architectural redesign. Accordingly, we propose an evaluation framework leveraging Pareto optimality to assess the sensitivity of traditional RS models to hyperparameter tuning in multi-objective scenarios. We test our framework through comprehensive experiments on six diverse RS models, spanning neighborhood-based, factorization-based, and graph-based methods. Specifically, we evaluate 32 hyperparameter settings for each model in two representative scenarios: (i) mitigating popularity bias in content exposure and (ii) jointly optimizing accuracy, novelty, and diversity in content delivery. We also analyze which hyperparameters matter most, offering actionable insights to practitioners aiming to balance objectives with limited implementation overhead. Overall, our findings indicate that hyperparameter optimization can provide a practical complementary pathway for improving multi-objective behavior in conventional RS models under the considered settings. Our results identify UserKNN as the most robust model, consistently requiring minimal tuning to achieve Pareto optimality. Conversely, factorization and graph-based models (e.g., LightGCN) show higher sensitivity, where increasing the embedding dimension (factors) emerges as the most critical lever for improving multi-objective trade-offs. We make the codes publicly available at: https://github.com/vincpapa/HP4MORec .
